newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks plunge on political worries.
newsitem.headline: French stocks plunge on political worries.

text.p: French shares came under attack on Friday as political worries led by speculation of an early parliamentary election or a cabinet reshuffle took center stage, brokers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended 67.62 points or 2.59 percent lower at 2,547.56. It had reached a low of 2,540.79 during the day.
The CAC-40 futures contract for April was down 14 points at 2,547. Total volume was a hefty eight billion francs.
"Prospects of an early election drove the market down," one broker said.
The absence of a firm official denial has allowed speculation to spread that the French parliament might be dissolved or the cabinet reshuffled.
A more buoyant mood on Wall Street failed to bring suppport in a session dominated by politics.
"This is a strictly domestic matter. New York is rising but the franc is weak. People here are focusing on politics," one dealer said.

Most brokers said the market was likely to remain volatile in coming days but said investors were not panicking though some worried snap elections may pave the way for a new austerity plan ahead of the transition to a single European currency.
Most blue chips were under pressure as both French and domestic investors hedged positions.
AGF ended down 2.46 percent to 194.5 francs. The French insurer declined to comment on a French newspaper report it planned to tap markets for four billlion francs because interest rates were low.

PSA Peugeot Citroen lost 4.09 percent to 586 francs. Several brokers cut their estimates for the group in 1997 and 1998 following disappointing 1996 results. Rival carmaker Renault closed down 5.66 percent to 130 francs.
